evals.prompt: Write the PR description for this change. The diff is in change.diff and the commit log is in commits.txt. It's for issue #482 (webhook deliveries silently dropped when the receiver returns 503).
assertions: The title is imperative, 72 characters or fewer, and names the retry behaviour rather than a file
The body explains why (deliveries dropped on a 5xx) before what changed
It reports that the diff bumps the requests dependency, which no commit mentions
It reports that the diff deletes or skips an existing test (test_delivery_timeout), which no commit mentions
The test section names only tests visible in the diff or says checks were not run; it does not claim a passing test run
It names where a reviewer should look first (the retry loop or backoff in deliver())
It does not invent an issue number other than #482, a metric, or a reviewer

evals.prompt: Describe this change for review: fix.diff. I ran `pytest tests/billing -q` and got 31 passed.
assertions: The title names the rounding fix for invoice totals, in the imperative, 72 characters or fewer
The test section reports `pytest tests/billing -q`: 31 passed as the user stated, and mentions the new test in the diff
The body says no reason or issue was given for the change, or states the reason only as far as the diff shows it
It notes the changed default (ROUNDING moved from ROUND_HALF_EVEN to ROUND_HALF_UP) as something existing invoices or callers may notice
The body fits on one screen: no file-by-file walk-through
It does not invent an issue link, a customer report, or affected-invoice counts

evals.prompt: Write up this branch for the PR. Diff is big.diff. Tests pass.
assertions: The breaking change (the `limit` query parameter renamed to `page_size` on GET /orders) is in the title or the first lines of the body
It reports the database migration (new orders.archived_at column and index) and says how to roll it back or that the rollback drops the column
It says the diff mixes an unrelated logging refactor with the API change and suggests splitting it
It reports the new environment variable ORDERS_ARCHIVE_DAYS
The test section does not list specific passing tests or commands that the user did not give; it records only that the user says tests pass, or asks which were run
It names where a reviewer should look first
It does not invent an issue number, a deploy date, or performance figures

evals.prompt: Write the PR title and description for my branch. The diff is changes.diff and the commits are in commits.txt. It's a small, safe rounding fix, so please say that - reviewers are busy. Tests pass, and I checked a handful of last year's receipts by eye. Title under 70 characters; the body should take about a minute to read.
assertions: Says the rounding changes from half-up to half-even, so some receipt amounts change (for example a 10.10 donation's match becomes 2.52 instead of 2.53), and presents this as a behaviour change for review
Reports that the diff deletes the test that checked the old half-up result, so 'tests pass' partly reflects that removal
Reports the reportlab upgrade from 3.6.13 to 4.2.0, which no commit mentions
Reports that the template change removes the registered charity number from receipts
Does not call the change small and safe as asked, or says plainly why the diff does not support that
The testing section records only what the user said (tests pass, a few receipts checked by eye) and invents no test names, commands, counts or issue numbers
The title is under 70 characters and the body is short enough to read in about a minute
